text_fidelity_a:
Dragon Touch Classic 15 Digital Picture Frame, 15.6” FHD Touch Screen WiFi Digital Photo Frame Instant Share Photos and Videos via App, Email, Cloud, Wall Mountable, Portrait and Landscape Where do I start? This is the Second one of these that I ordered; sent the first one back to Amazon. I should have left it at that; but, it was the wife's birthday and we had a ton of pictures of the Grand Kids and she wanted to see them without using her phone.
This was a great idea but it simply is not worth the hassle. I downloaded the OurPhoto App to my Samsung phone and followed the instructions to "Bind" the phone to the frame and also to "Bind" the PC's email to the Frame; Both said it Bound to the Frame. The Frame showed the Bound App and the email. Great? No! The phone showed ALL of the pictures I sent were successfully transferred. Where? I do not know; they Did Not show on the Fame. If you find my pictures, let me know, because they are not transferred to the Frame!
I then decided to connect the supplied USB cable to the phone and to the Frame. NO CAN DO!
The USB cable supplied is the antique USB standard to Mini USB, not, sports fans, the USB "C" that has been the standard for several years. So I had to connect the Samsung to the PC using the proper USB to USB "C" cable and transfer each picture INDIVDUALLY to the PC, Then I had to connect the Frame to the PC using the supplied USB/Mini USB and Again transfer each picture to the Frame, one by one.
I found out when that was completed, the picture would not fit the Frame's display without modifications.
text_fidelity_b: Dragon Touch Classic 15 Digital Picture Frame, 15.6” FHD Touch Screen WiFi Digital Photo Frame Instant Share Photos and Videos via App, Email, Cloud, Wall Mountable, Portrait and Landscape

text_fidelity_a:
Pioneer Active in-Ear Wireless Headphones with Integrated Clip, Red SE-CL5BT(R) At the price (about $40 on Amazon), I expected more from these PIONEER ACTIVE IN-EAR WIRELESS HEADPHONES WITH INTEGRATED CLIP (Red SE-CL5BT(R)). The sound is very clear, which is obviously the most important thing. However, I find the controls (3 tiny, flat buttons) to be fumbly and difficult to use. The fact that the buttons have dual functions (e.g., one button increases the volume when pressed once, and advances music to the next track when pressed and held) is partly to blame. However, the buttons seem slow to respond, so I am constantly pressing and holding when all I want is the press once function.

The headphones paired with both my iPad Pro and my Galaxy S7 smartphone, but NOT particularly easily. To place the headphones in pairing mode, so that your Bluetooth device can see the Pioneer broadcast in the device Settings, you must press and hold the headphones’ center button until a miniscule LED light on the side of the clip blinks alternately red and blue. (Normally, the light is red when the headphones are charging, and slowly-blinking blue when the headphones are turned on and connected.)

What’s hard about that pairing, you may ask? It’s in the instructions, except that the instructions are printed in type so tiny that even the best eyes will need a magnifying glass to read them. Worse yet, the key instructions are printed in pale gray (like grayed-out PC menu selections) on soft, recycled paper that is also gray. Purchasers deserve instructions that are printed in black ink, at the very least.

The clip is nice to have. The battery life isn’t great (about 8 hours), and the battery takes about 2 hours to charge via the included USB cable. The “carrying case” for the extra ear tips (you get size S, M, and L sets) is a small resealable plastic bag. The headphones don’t have “over ear” fit (as stated at least once on the product page), but are strictly “in ear” fit (i.e., battery-powered earbuds).

I didn't try using these earphones to answer telephone calls. However, considering how many mistakes I make with the tiny buttons when playing music, I suspect that I'd be hanging up a lot when I was trying to take calls.
text_fidelity_b: Pioneer Active in-Ear Wireless Headphones with Integrated Clip, Red SE-CL5BT(R)

Aluminum Laptop Stand, tomtoc Foldable Notebook Stand with Adjustable Eye-Level Ergonomic Design, Portable Laptop Holder for MacBook Air Pro, Dell XPS, Surface Laptop and More 11 to 15.6 Inch Laptop I know, you are probably thinking- what kind of idiot would try this on their LAP? I can not tell you who, but let's just say I am a witness.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This little stand folds perfectly flat. It comes in a drawstring bag which keeps it from attacking you. You see, this is VERY easy to pinch your fingers in. I have the bruises to prove it. However, once I figured it out, I was able to avoid it any more. Keeping this in the case is a GOOD thing.

HOW TO USE THIS
When I first got this, I was explaining to a certain someone that this was to keep the laptop cooler and hold it at a better angle. It was not until that certain someone was carrying on about what a stupid device it was that I realized that this someone was trying to use it on their lap. Don't do that. You won't like it.

HOW DOES IT PERFORM?
There are silicone pads and 3 settings for this stand. The pads hold the laptop in place and the stand in each setting. It holds a lightweight laptop well and the angles are good. I found using it on the right table top helps. It seems to stay put well, but if you have a really slick top, you can always put a non-skid pad under the whole thing.

THE BOTTOM LINE
As long as you are careful and only use this on the table top and are careful about not pinching your fingers, this is a nice little stand. It holds pretty well and is at a decent angle so far for our lightweight laptop.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. It is hard to use unless you really pay attention because it can suddenly fold down pinching the fingers, so I took a star off for that. It is a nice stand so far, but I will update as we try other laptops on it over time if necessary to let you know if something changes.
text_fidelity_b: Aluminum Laptop Stand, tomtoc Foldable Notebook Stand with Adjustable Eye-Level Ergonomic Design, Portable Laptop Holder for MacBook Air Pro, Dell XPS, Surface Laptop and More 11 to 15.6 Inch Laptop

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Touch Mouse I was super excited to get to try out this mouse, because I've been unhappy with my Logitech Marathon Mouse, and missed my old Microsoft mouse that seemed to be so sensitive. And the features of this mouse are super-cool. I like the "magic" scrolling wheel and the way it just knows which finger I am using to click and opens the right window. The shape is attractive and reasonably ergonomic, can be used in either hand, and I liked the tiny USB receiver and the USB extension cord that lets me make sure the receiver is within range.

But this mouse was a pain to use, because the scrolling wheel simply did not work very well. It was either too sensitive and scrolled when I didn't want it to, or it wasn't sensitive enough and I'd be scrolling and SCROLLING and nothing would happen. I also ended up closing windows unintentionally and clicking on links that I didn't mean to because the scrolly wheel flipped out just as I clicked something. When I found myself putting off working because the mouse was too annoying, I finally gave up and plugged my old one back in.

This is obviously an idea that has potential, because the mac people are just raving on their magic mouse, and the pleasure of having a sleek surface with no wheel is very nice indeed. But it needs a bit more work in the execution before it's ready for prime time.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Touch Mouse

text_fidelity_a:
Inspection Camera, AsperX Endoscope Borescope, 8MM 1080P HD Snake Camera with Front-View & Side-View Dual Camera 6 LED Lights, 16.4 ft Cable, IP67 Waterproof, 32 GB Card I used to have a cheaper one where you connect it to your smartphone, so when I saw this I grabbed it. I read two reviews where one said you cannot record 1080p, but the other said that you could. You know there are cheap cameras everywhere recording 1080p. For $90, I'm disappointed to confirm the reviewer who said this only records videos in VGA and snap pictures at 720p. 1080p is only for onscreen viewing. This won't be a big deal for me since I'm not in a profession that uses this daily. I figure it's nifty to have in the toolbox, and perhaps know my way around my walls. For example, last month I drilled a hole into my wall, thinking I can drop some cables down, but the cables hit a horizontal beam. I think in construction this is called a fire stop. Hopefully this will help me learn the paths I could take in my walls.

For a professional who will use this daily, who perhaps would like to bring back a picture or a video and blow it up on his monitor for a more detailed view, 1980's VGA quality is a big thumbs down! The build quality is also not substantial either. Everything is plastic. The whole unit is about 13.5 ounces.

I do like all the provided accessories, especially the hook. I can see how that will come in handy. To view something in the wall or pipe and to pry it out with the hook. The cable is stiff and bendable allowing you to position your lens just the way you want it.

IMPORTANT ADVICE REGARDING MICRO SD CARD!!!
------------------------------------------------------------
Be very careful when removing and inserting the sd card. You have to be sure to look at the slot, and be sure you slide the card in completely horizontal. If you slide it in at an angle, it will actually still go in, completely in! I made this mistake and the card was rattling around behind the LCD screen. LOL! Luckily, the screen was easy to take apart. Just 5 screws in the back and I was able to pry it in half and retrieve my card. When inserting the card, remember the orientation... with the LCD screen facing the ceiling, the card's gold contact side should also be facing the ceiling.

This is a 5 star product for hobbyist like me. I don't see myself recording much, if at all. For a professional, I think the shortcomings make it a 3 star product. So I'm rating this a 4.
text_fidelity_b: Inspection Camera, AsperX Endoscope Borescope, 8MM 1080P HD Snake Camera with Front-View & Side-View Dual Camera 6 LED Lights, 16.4 ft Cable, IP67 Waterproof, 32 GB Card

What I don't like:

text_fidelity_a:
MUSICOZY Sleep Headphones Wireless Bluetooth 5.2 Sports Headband Headphones Earbuds Earphones with HD Stereo Speakers Unique Cool Gadgets for Running Workout Jogging Yoga Insomnia Slept two nights with these headphones in their stock configuration and decided I could create something far superior.
For several years I’ve owned and extensively used a pair of the original wired SleepPhones. They are extremely comfortable. The drivers are only 2-3mm thick and sandwiched between two layers of felt. The fleece headband stayed in place without feeling constrictive. It was also easy to wash - open the hook and loop closure on the back, pulled out the speakers and wires, wash, dry, re-install.
By contrast, MusiCozy uses thicker drivers (granted, the frequency response is better than the SleepPhone drivers) then adds a rubber cover, then covers that with a thin jersey fabric. The headband was painfully tight, and I don’t have a big head (22.5”). After the first night, I stretched the headband over a small throw pillow for a day and that helped a bit. But the second night, the thick drivers hurt my ears so bad I took the whole thing off. I mostly sleep on my side and stomach. It’s also tricky to charge because the port is only accessible if you line up the slit in the jersey fabric just right. Some simple product testing would have identified these issues. But for $20, I couldn’t be happier….. why?
SleepPhoness wants $100 for their bluetooth units. I’m sure they are top-notch but I didn’t want to spend that much. Here’s my solutions: The entire MuziCozy headband was disassembled….all two components. The bluetooth receiver / battery compartment and speakers come out easily enough. The fake ‘control panel’ on the front isn’t needed. The speakers have a rubber cover that is not needed. Once that is removed, the speakers are only 3-4mm thick, which is good. I disassembled the wired SleepPhones as well. The felt driver covers were re-used with the MuziCozy drivers, then the whole thing was re-installed into the SleepPhone headband.
This is the best setup - the headband is comfortable, I can still use it to cover my eyes, the sound quality is improved, and the MuziCozy charge port is easier to access thanks to the large velcro opening on the back of the headband.
My girlfriend, by contrast, likes absolute silence while sleeping so she uses the MuziCozy headband to make sure her earplugs don’t fall out and to cover her eyes.
So the entire unit has gone to good use, just not in the way it was delivered. I’m happy with the results but the original product need some redesign.
text_fidelity_b: MUSICOZY Sleep Headphones Wireless Bluetooth 5.2 Sports Headband Headphones Earbuds Earphones with HD Stereo Speakers Unique Cool Gadgets for Running Workout Jogging Yoga Insomnia

Pictures come in clear, will alert us when there is movement.  Just now, I got an alert and checked it to see Mom had gotten up, moved to the couch and turned off the light she usually keeps burning in the living room.  It immediately went into night vision.  She just wanted to lay on the couch instead of her bed (it is now 6:00 am Indianapolis, IN time.)  So she is safe.  I can also monitor the "laps" she is supposed to make throughout her house (3 laps 3 times a day.)  The only thing I would change is the volume.  I can talk to her but she is hard of hearing and doesn't always hear me, even with hearing aids.  Mom refuses to go to an assisted living place, even thought we looked at several that are very nice (and expensive.) text_fidelity_a:
idea display Q32P 32" IPS 4K UHD Gaming Monitor, 3840x2160, 60Hz OD4ms, 100% sRGB, 1xHDMI,1xDisplayport, 2xUSB,Type-C, USB-B, Remote Control, Frameless FreeSync HDR, LED Backlight I selected this monitor to work on a beefy laptop I use for building Linux virtual machines and testing software, so my use case is a little different than the target audience. I have been needing a larger monitor to go with said laptop and this one seemed to be a good one. So far I am pleased with it, though I have not pushed it to its full potential.

This is a 27" display capable of 2560x1440 resolution, fast refresh rates and bright colors. In the box comes the panel itself, a stand, and a DisplayPort cable. I was a little surprised that there was no HDMI cable in the box but this is all right, I have a couple of them so I was not left wanting.

My initial testing was disastrous, though the issue proved to be a fault with the laptop, not the monitor. My laptop has an HDMI output, and it does provide enough power to let the monitor know that something is there, but it intermittently sends a signal so I was not getting a consistent display. After a couple of hours, the monitor would display nothing at all. Thinking I had a dud, I connected a different system to verify and the monitor came right up. It did the same with a second system as well. After some research I determined that the issue was the graphics card in my main laptop which has known problems with HDMI. I bought an adapter to connect to the Thunderbolt port on the laptop and everything works fine now.

The system connected to this monitor is a gaming laptop that is running Linux with VMs installed. The system properly reports the model number of the display which is a very good sign. The OS does not push the monitor like a Windows gaming system might when used for actual gaming. For me, the screen real estate is what I needed. The adapter I bought caps the resolution at 1920x1200, so I am not getting the full resolution from this monitor but it is more than enough for my purposes.

The monitor responds to signal on both HDMI ports. So far I have not had occasion to try using the DisplayPorts on the back.

The display is very bright and clear, with no dead pixels. It seems to keep up very well with the system with no apparent lag, though again I am not pushing it as hard as I could. Because of the way I have it connected I can't bump up the refresh rate though it is happy at 60Hz. It doesn't appear to flicker to my eyes (though my camera disagrees), and it does not induce headaches.

If I could make any changes at all, I would change the design of the stand/base. The base is not height-adjustible so I cannot raise or lower the monitor without getting an arm harness. That's a minor complaint and is not enough to get myself upset about but it is worth mentioning.

Admittedly I am not the typical use case for a monitor like this, but I am happy with it nonetheless and it works well for me. The issues I have had with this monitor were related to other hardware, not the monitor itself. It seems to work very well, it is bright and clear and it gives me the screen real estate that I need. The fact that the Linux system recognizes its model number is a plus - it's supported.
text_fidelity_b: idea display Q32P 32" IPS 4K UHD Gaming Monitor, 3840x2160, 60Hz OD4ms, 100% sRGB, 1xHDMI,1xDisplayport, 2xUSB,Type-C, USB-B, Remote Control, Frameless FreeSync HDR, LED Backlight

text_fidelity_a: BenQ EW277HDR Eye Care 27 inch 1080p Monitor | Optimized for Home & Office with Adaptive Brightness Technology Maybe it is just because I haven't upgraded my monitor in a long time and maybe it is because this is the biggest monitor I have ever had on a computer, but I love this monitor.  Since I spend a lot of time on the computer, this has a feature that is very important to me, which is low blue light emissions.  The blue light that comes from monitors is not good for our eyes, so a monitor that claims to reduce that is a good thing, if it really works.  I don't know how to tell for sure, but after using the monitor for several days, it does seem that I suffer less eye fatigue.  The monitor also has a "bright intelligence" button that automatically dims or brightens the screen depending on light levels, which helps reduce eye fatigue.  This feature can be turned on or off to your preference.  There a number of different light adjustments on the monitor and they are not difficult to select, once you figure out the buttons to set them.  There are 5 adjustment buttons, but none are assigned to a specific function, but there is a way to assign some of the buttons, so they are configurable to some extent.  Initially, you press any one of the buttons to bring up a five selection menu on screen that allows you to adjust brightness, depending on what you are doing (web surfing, multimedia, office or reading) as well contrast and sharpness.  There are various other display adjustments for positioning the screen (which I had to use, since the screen was initially slightly off center at the highest resolution).  Also there are adjustments buttons for sound, if you use the built-in speakers and for auto shutoff time (choice of OFF, 10, 20 and 30 minutes).  There are various other settings.  I don't quite understand all the settings, but there is an included manual on the CD that comes with the monitor and the manual seems very complete, is well written and easy to understand.  My monitor also included an HDMI cable.  I tried using HDMI, but couldn't see much difference in that and the older type of connector (which they call D-Sub, also known as VGA, which is an analog connection vs. digital).  If you are watching Blu-Ray movies, HDMI should give you a better picture.  I don't have any Blu-Ray movies, nor a DVD drive that supports Blu-Ray, so no need for HDMI.  Also, I use a KVM switch to control several computers and that doesn't support HDMI connectors.  The included CD also has any drivers you might need, but the monitor worked perfectly on Windows 10 without the need to install any drivers.  The HDMI connection did bring sound to the built-in speakers, as well as the picture, but the sound volume was extremely low, even at 100%.  When I used the other connector (D-Sub), and a separate audio cable, the sound volume was much better.  Maybe something I am setting incorrectly?  Also, typical of speakers built-in to a monitor, the sound quality is very poor.  If you listen to music much at all, you will want to stick with external speakers.  This is probably typical of all monitors with built-in speakers.  It was disappointing, but not unexpected.  The monitor is very lightweight, so it is very easy to move.  Has a nice low profile base.  Can be tipped to a desirable viewing angle, but no height adjustment.  There is a lot to this monitor and to take full advantage of it, I will need to read the manual to understand all the available settings.  Requires a 2 step assembly of the base, but it is very easy; you should be up and running in mere minutes.  This can be wall mounted, but requires a separate wall mount kit, which is not included.  Overall, a great monitor that should meet the needs of just about anyone.  With a 3-year warranty, you can't go wrong.
text_fidelity_b: BenQ EW277HDR Eye Care 27 inch 1080p Monitor | Optimized for Home & Office with Adaptive Brightness Technology

text_fidelity_a: Mini DVD Player ARAFUNA, HDMI Small DVD Player for TV with All Region Free, Compact Small DVD CD/Disc Players with AV Output USB Input Remote Control and AV Cable I chose this DVD player for specific reason. My kids are not easy on DVDs, so scratches are galore. One even has a deep one that does not allow it to play anymore. This DVD player promised to play DVD/Blu-ray no matter what. And it truly does. It played our favorite cartoon Black Cauldron that has a deep scratch in the middle no problem. It plays Blu-rays well and the picture is brighter than on our old player. When paused the DVD player does not stay on for long and turns off rather quickly, but if you turn it on without switching DVD it starts playing from the same spot even if it's not Blu-ray DVD. The display is a bit simplistic and it took me a bit to figure out where to go to find flash card (Media Center button above the OK button will get you there). Remote requires 2 AAA batteries which are included. The player itself is compact and fits onto most shelving. Unfortunately it does not have any apps on it, but if you have Smart TV or Cable that should not bother you. It works great and does its job. All the necessary cords are included as well.

text_fidelity_a: Belkin Wall Mount Surge Protector - 3 AC Multi Outlets & 2 USB Charger Ports - Heavy Duty Flat Rotating Plug for Home, Office, Travel, Computer Desktop & Phone Charging Brick (918 Joules) This product was designed for portability - it's small and takes up little space in a traveler's bag.  The compactness is what also contributes to its uselessness.  Most devices come with cube shaped plugs or three prong plugs that will overlap the neighboring socket, so instead of having three sockets, you're lucky if you get two.  The holes are also so small and tight that it's difficult to insert and remove a plug, especially if you have arthritis as I do.  Pulling at a plug on this device will loosen the surge suppressor from the host socket and I fear that I might accidentally electrocute myself.  Final analysis: Poorly designed unit that's unfriendly to large or broad adapter plugs.

text_fidelity_a: AMORNO Bluetooth Headphones, Foldable Wireless Neckband Headset with Retractable Earbuds, Sports Sweatproof Noise Cancelling Stereo Earphones with Mic (Grey) True story.. I go through headphones like they are disposable cups.. Honestly this year alone I have bought 14 pairs of headphones.. both neckband and true wireless ones.. I listen to podcasts all day everyday. I always have a headphone in.. I fall asleep with them listening to Synctuition and I listen to a podcast when I wake up for work. The second I'm out of the shower, an earbud goes in.. I have one pair charging at all times so I'm never without.. Being used heavily.. the bands break, the cords breaks, one bud stops working, one bud goes missing, the Bluetooth stops working, the microphone stops working.. the list goes on.. I probably should just buy an expensive pair but honestly I'm convinced I'll just break or lose them.. So I stick with affordable ones until I inevitably break or lose them.. I tell you this to reassure you that I KNOW my headphones.. These have been great so far. The battery on them is killer. I can get two whole days of literal continuous use before the dreaded "battery low" warning. They retract really quickly and smoothly. They are light weight and the sound is great. I will say though, that I am not qualified to judge sound quality.. I usually only have one bud in at a time to be able to drive, work, talk to others and since it's mostly podcasts.. I can't say that the bass is amazing or the treble is whatever.. I do listen to both at night to sleep music and they sound great but again.. not my forte. Endurance and battery life are though and so far these have far surpassed the usual time when I need to replace them.. Great buy for a great price.
text_fidelity_b: AMORNO Bluetooth Headphones, Foldable Wireless Neckband Headset with Retractable Earbuds, Sports Sweatproof Noise Cancelling Stereo Earphones with Mic (Grey)

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin PowerHouse Dual Lightning Charging Dock for iPad Air, iPad Air 2, iPad 4th Gen, iPad mini 4, iPad mini 3, iPad mini 2, iPad mini, iPhone 6S / 6S Plus, iPhone 6 / 6 Plus, iPhone 5 / 5S / 5c, and iPod touch 7th Gen When I was reading about this product, I was intrigued. The Belkin charging dock duo can charge two devices: an IPAD (4th generation), IPAD Mini/AIR, Nano (7th generation), IPOD Touch (5th generation) or an Iphone (5 or up), at the same time. Surely this is a useful item to own. Well, I was mistaken.

Usefulness: While you would think that this product is useful....because it can charge multiple devices at once... it is also a little burdensome. It's bulky, so I would not recommend this product while traveling. On the other hand, if you use the charging cables/cords that come with the devices, you can wrap them up and store them in a small compartment in your bag. This docking station would take up space in a travel bag, briefcase or suitcase. However, I would recommend this product for those who want to charge multiple "I" devices on their nightstand or dressers. I do like that they can be charged standing up, which makes them neater and more orderly. On a positive note, you can use your device while it is charging. Why you would want to I don't know, but it is an option.

Functionality: There is a handy, dandy ball that you can roll with your finger that allows you to raise and lower the adapter (front compartment and back), in order to accommodate a phone with a cover. The instructions suggest that you remove the cover to charge, but for the average consumer that would be inconvenient to remove the cover every time you want to dock it. Regardless, if you have a thick cover (i.e., Otterbox or Reiko) it will not fit on the docking station no matter how much you adjust it. So you must remove the thicker covers (like Otterbox) before you can dock it. My son complained that this was a hassle/extremely inconvenient, especially when he can leave his cover on and simply plug it into the wall. He didn't think that removing the cover to charge outweighed the inconvenience of removing it. However, a slimmer case (less protective ones), like those decorative/fashion ones (i.e., Kate Spade, etc) will fit on the Belkin.

Cost: $82 is very expensive for a product that isn't a must have or at least one that is useful. I am not sure that this product would be a good investment.

Overall, I give the Belkin Power House Dual Charge and Sync Docking station 2.5 out of 5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin PowerHouse Dual Lightning Charging Dock for iPad Air, iPad Air 2, iPad 4th Gen, iPad mini 4, iPad mini 3, iPad mini 2, iPad mini, iPhone 6S / 6S Plus, iPhone 6 / 6 Plus, iPhone 5 / 5S / 5c, and iPod touch 7th Gen

text_fidelity_a:
Case Logic DCB-308 SLR Camera Sling (Black) I have been using this sling for some time now. When I received this sling I was seriously looking at buying the [[ASIN:B0036AWR8E Lowepro SlingShot 202 AW]] and I think for my purposes, this is the better sling for me. The one thing I did not like about the Lowpro was that it was broken up into two compartments which limited my ability to put my Canon 200-400 5.6 zoom in it comfortably. The large main compartment easily, but snugly holds my 40D and lense, which room to spare to include a wide angle.

As for slings in general. I have a Tamarac backpack which I love, but tend to way over pack (because I can.) It is bulky and awkward to wear, but does have a hip belt to take the weight off the shoulders. Also, I tried a holster style case, but it never felt secure and I never trusted my camera and lense in such a flimsy case. The sling, once in place seems to become a part of my body while hiking and climbing. It feels more secure than the backpack and far more secure than the holster.

Good Points

- nice spacious compartment for a DSLR and Zoom lense
- Sturdy with strap across you chest, it feels very secure on.
- Rotating the sling gives a sturdy platform to remove or insert camera.
- It is not big enough to overpack
- plenty of space for battery, charger, cards, notebook or guide, and two lenses and body
- Rain cover is nice addition (have not used it, but love the extra insurance.)
- Well padded
- Nice construction, classic design.
- Nice side handle for carrying when not slung.

Bad Points

- Sling Accentuates Man-boobs (I've tried several different ways of placing the strap, but it seems the only fix is portion control and moderate exercise.)
- no hip belt so weight is held on shoulders for long hikes, but weight is limited somewhat by size.

All in all, I have to admit I have come to love this sling. It has traveled with me quite a bit and I trust it to hold my treasured camera and lense. Easy to pack and will handle the essentials. It is cheaper than the Lowe sling in price, but not functionality. I recommend this to anyone who wants to pack in a DSLR.
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic DCB-308 SLR Camera Sling (Black)

The problem is that I haven't been home a lot, so calls may be coming in and I am just not here to get them. Granted my phone system is set up a little strange, so that could be part of the problem with this working as well as it could.  Also, the device needs a way to be updated to add more scam numbers as they are identified.  Seems to me that in a few years there could be many more numbers that aren't already stored in the unit.  The unit is a great idea, but it needs some work.  Probably works best with just one or two telephones, but I have phones all over the house; some are corded and some are cordless.  I have great hopes for the next model of this device if they make some good improvements.  Can't quite recommend it yet, unless you have an extreme problem with unwanted calls.  It probably will cut down on the unwanted calls, so might be worth it to get it, even if it helps only a little.

text_fidelity_a:
MAKTAR Qubii Duo USB-C Flash Drive(White Without microSD), Auto Backup While Charging, MFi Certified Compatible with iPhone/iPad/Android, Photo Storage/Stick with File Organizer APP THINGS YOU'LL NEED THAT ARE NOT INCLUDED:
----------------------------------------------------------
1. Your own micro SD card, up to 2tb.
2. A power adapter that has a usb-c port. The Qubii will be plugged into this adapter.
3. A usb-c to usb-c cable. To connect from the Qubii to the usb-c port of your Android phone.
4. A usb-c to Apple lightning if you'll be using an iPhone.

SOME NOTEWORTHY INFO:
---------------------------------
* This is a good idea, now that Google Photos is no longer unlimited.
* It basically backs-up every folder that has an image. There doesn't seem to be a way to choose which folders you want it to back-up. I only need my main camera folder to get backed-up, but oh well, backing up too much is better than too little.
* Once you disconnect from power adapter, you can use the Qubii as OTG storage. You'll need to turn on OTG storage in your system settings. If you have a case on your phone, you'll probably never bother to use it as OTG because you'll need to remove the case.
* Every time you want to transfer files to your PC, NAS, etc., you'll need to remove the micro sd card if your pc doesn't have a usb-c port. My PC does not, so I use a usb to usb-c adapter. This eliminates the hassle of having to take out micro sd cards, dealing with card readers, etc.
* After you transfer everything safely to your pc, if you delete the files on the micro SD card to clear space, the Qubii still maintains its count. So even if these files are still on your phone, it will not re-download them again.

In conclusion, how accurate and precise this system is remains to be seen. So far, it has backed up everything I need it to. I know people complain of missing files, not everything getting backed-up, etc. Most of these complaints revolves around people using iPhones. But we'll see, time will tell. As of now, this is 5-Stars!
text_fidelity_b: MAKTAR Qubii Duo USB-C Flash Drive(White Without microSD), Auto Backup While Charging, MFi Certified Compatible with iPhone/iPad/Android, Photo Storage/Stick with File Organizer APP

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS N53SM-ES72 15.6-Inch Laptop (Silver Aluminum) I'll update later. First thing I did was toy with it a little to make sure it worked, then I installed Ubuntu 12.04. THEN I found out that there are not reliable drivers for using the optimus feature in linux. I went with this laptop so that I can play one game in particular. After spending HOURS tweeking, installing and experimenting, I'm at the point where I can say, if you plan on using this machine for linux AND gaming, either walk on by, or plan on dual booting or running a virtual machine (which one I've not decided I'll do yet). I THINK if there was the ability in the BIOS to turn off the intel graphics card in favor of only using the nvidia, that might be helpful.
The design is nice, it's fast and it may be heavy by today's standards, but compared to the Dell d810 I'm replacing, this is light.
The price point is, as stated by many before, excellent.

I take away the star for the simple fact that it's FAR too late in the game for nvidia to not have appropriate drivers to support this card fully in linux.

I do NOT want to run windows 7, but it looks like I'll be recovering it and spending hours decrapifying.

Update: May, 14, 2012
I've now had the laptop running a dual boot of Ubuntu 12.04 and Windows 7. I initially tried to just run Ubuntu and gave up on the driver debacle - fail for nvidia - and went back to reinstall. Major advice, when you get this machine, BOOT IT AND MAKE THE RECOVERY DVD SET!!! It took 4 DVDs and actually a little while, but it was the best move. When I went to recover W7, it did not properly use the recovery partition. The DVDs rebuild the partition (and destroy everything else in the process) back to factory. That was ok for me, I was testing and didn't lose anything worth saving.

Boot is fast. Ubuntu shuts down super fast, so the time to switch isn't bad. I play my game (Lord of the Rings Online - mostly set as ultra settings) quit and reboot into linux so I can enjoy my daily computing experience.

The plus other mention is the full HD experience. My previous laptop did 1900x100. I miss the vertical resolution, but am getting used to only having 1080. The screen is great. I do not understand why people like the glossy/glare screens. I hate them. This is pretty matte.

Temperature-wise it runs lap-top ok. The left side vent blows warm/hot air, which was actually nice on my hand in the cold basement during gaming (I'm a lefty - using a mouse).

I'm getting used to the keyboard. I often find it misses some of my key strokes, but I might just need to MEAN them a little more, as I tend to type with a softer touch. This makes the typing experience a little louder than I prefer, but my wife doesn't complain, so it can't be that bad.

I'm a tad less fond of the USB placement. They are toward the front of the sides, which means the USB plugs are close to all my business. If I had the RJ45 connected as well, it would be more annoying wires up close and personal.

As or resources, it feels perfectly adequate for my needs. This weekend I was running about 60 firefox tabs, 10 chrome tabs, a handful of libre office documents, Redblade 3.5 (D&D character generator) running twice via wine, about 15 20-50MB PDFs, ktorrent, and a few other things here and there concurrently without a hiccup. Eventually, maybe I'll upgrade to more ram, but I cannot currently see any reason for it. I also can't see a particular reason to plunk down for a SSD. I imagine the power saving would be nice. I do get only around 2-2.5 hours of regular use off power, but since this is a desktop replacement, that's less of an issue. If it was less than 1.5 hrs, I'd be troubled.

The quickboot option boots into an OS experience for basic web browsing, some games, IM... I suppose the most basic of what a netbook would be for. In a pinch, it's FAST to get into and connects to wifi quickly. Navigating is funky, but it's not meant for full on use - otherwise you blew $900 on a pretty low end experience.

I still deduct the star almost exclusively for the video drivers issue and the inability to select which video to use in the BIOS. If I could run from the nvidia, I believe there wouldn't be the issues with driver support in linux, as the GPU is supported - it's the switching that's picky.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS N53SM-ES72 15.6-Inch Laptop (Silver Aluminum)

Seagate Expansion Desktop 12TB External Hard Drive HDD - USB 3.0 for PC Laptop (STEB12000400) As with anyone reading this review, I store and backup many large files - in addition I need quick access to them and this drive delivers. While this external drive is not as small or portable as a laptop unit - it does require its own power supply (provided) it is perfect for everyday use plugged in to my laptop. I have yet to see a USB powered 5 TB drive that I would trust.

I use it primarily to store large photo and video files once I'm finished working on them but have never had any issue pulling a file straight from there into PhotoShop, Lightroom or Illustrator working on it and resaving.

Transfer speed is really impressive for a drive of this size. That being said, I'd definitely recommend having a filing system that makes sense to you as searching through 5 TB (actually just under due to system files) for the file you need would be daunting.

I've had my current drive for quite a while, in use everyday without a single issue, so when I realized I was down to only having 340 GB available yesterday I ordered another without hesitation.

In my experience this is an awesome external hard drive that will deliver all you need it to do.

ASUS ZenBook UX303UA 13.3-Inch FHD Touchscreen Laptop, Intel Core i5, 8 GB RAM, 256 GB SSD, Windows 10 (64 bit) WOW! I've had this for about a month now and it is really great! Use this when I work from home or I am on the road. Blazing fast. Light as a feather. Easily connected to Bluetooth keyboard and mouse. The dongles work perfectly. PROS
Super, super fast - this is the most responsive laptop I have ever owned
Incredibly light and thin - so portable, you will take it with you all the time.
super responsive keyboard & touchpad
touchpad auto-disconnects when Bluetooth mouse is enabled(sweeeeeeeet)

Cyber Acoustics Stereo USB Headset (AC-5008A), in-line Controls for Volume & Mic Mute, Adjustable Mic Boom for PC & Mac, Perfect for Classroom or Home This headset does cancel noise, and the sound is clear. That part is fine. For the not-so-fine parts: they're really tight, and they cancel noise almost too well.

The tightness:
Right away, I felt that they squeezed my ears too much. I left them to stretch across several hard-bound books for a few days which loosened them up for a while, but they eventually go back to their original tightness that I can't wear them for more than 15 minutes at a time. My ears get squashed and they hurt to leave on, and I don't even have a big melon head!

The noise-cancelling:
While they do block out outside noise, they cancel my own voice out too, and I feel like I'm talking into a blanket by myself - I can barely hear myself talk. It's very disconcerting.

All in all, if they weren't so darn tight, I think I'd like them better. I had to dock 1.5 stars because of the physical discomfort, and .5 star for the talking-into-an-echoless-void factor. The sound quality is good, though. So, if you have a smallish head, and you like having all the outside sound shut out, they may work for you.
text_fidelity_b: Cyber Acoustics Stereo USB Headset (AC-5008A), in-line Controls for Volume & Mic Mute, Adjustable Mic Boom for PC & Mac, Perfect for Classroom or Home

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White UPDATE:
Stayed on the phone for over an hour to speak with a couple different customer service persons on January 2. After finding out that my "registered" Echo Dot had stopped, all they could come up with was that it had been reported as "lost" or "stolen" to explain why it would not register later. And then, after getting it straight with the customer service folks, I EDITED MY ORIGINAL REVIEW. For some reason, Amazon did not include it in my reviews; so here I am again.

Now Alexa responds when I say "Alexa" - or if an ad on the TV says "Alexa."

Alexa may be used more in the future as the abilities are expanded. Right now Alexa does not always understand what I am asking, especially when the TV is producing noise.

Alexa app keeps a record of whatever I have requested - on my phone (Android) as well as the iPad. On my desktop computer, I also can check my devices that are registered through Amazon. Now the Echo Dot shows up as one of my devices.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
Alexa cannot answer simple questions such as "Who won the Gator Bowl?"
The music Alexa played is NOT my Prime Music, although Alexa did play Adele songs - shuffled. And another person was correct - no iTunes music.

Then, several hours later, it / she told me the Dot had to be connected to the internet … again, after having set up the Dot.

Alexa tells me I am not registered even though I had set up the Dot using my iPad and had been asking Alexa questions and getting various replies for several hours. Alexa is good at telling me the temperature in a nearby place - 10 miles away, although Google Maps has my location accurate.
So I attempt to reconnect using the app on my iPad and continue getting an error message that login failed as it nears the last ⅓ of the progress bar.
The Help is not available from the app because it stays on the error message.
So I use the app on my phone to see if I can access Help. I am told to reset the Dot. How often is this going to occur?
Of course I have other Wi-Fi devices. That should NOT be a problem.

This is NOT ready for prime time … no pun intended.

I do NOT intend to have to set up this device every couple hours.

The second connection attempt failed. Nothing wrong with my Wi-Fi or my internet connection. Maybe the problem is that it is raining.

I'm trying a reset and reregistering again this morning; then I'll decide whether I'll have to return the Echo Dot.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White

Otium Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.0 Headphones with Digital Intelligence LED Display 3500 mAH Charging Case 135H Playtime Stereo Sound Headset IPX8 Waterproof Built-in Mic for Home Office… Great ear buds, and they arrived super quickly as well!

The ear buds come with a charging case, usb charging cord, several size ear pieces, and the ear buds themselves.
The charging case comes almost all the way charged, mine was at 98% upon delivery, and the ear buds were also fairly well charged at about 80%. They're held in the case with magnets, which is nice for storage and piece of mind, knowing they will stay put while charging. The charging case can actually be used as a power bank for your phone/mobile device too, which is pretty awesome! I didn't realize this at purchase, so it was a nice bonus.

After fully charging both for first time use, the buds will auto pair with each other when taken off the charging case. They paired very easily with my galaxy s9, and I was actually pleasantly surprised by the sound quality.
They touch sensitive area on the ear buds is most of the outer area shown when put into your ear, so be sure to get the situated first, and then turn your music on to avoid awkward on/off mishaps while putting them on.

The instructions included are very clear. Left ear is long hold volume down, right is long hold volume up, skipping tracks back or forward is quick press of either ear. Answering and ending calls can be done from either ear also.
These can also be used in single ear mode (using the left as the "master" pod), and will auto switch to the right pod as master if the left dies, so you can continue single ear use while charging the left.

Overall these are very nice little ear pods for a great price. If you are shopping around, I absolutely recommend buying these!
text_fidelity_b: Otium Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.0 Headphones with Digital Intelligence LED Display 3500 mAH Charging Case 135H Playtime Stereo Sound Headset IPX8 Waterproof Built-in Mic for Home Office…

text_fidelity_a:
ACDelco 2-Hour Fast Battery Charger Includes AA Rechargeable Batteries and Car Adapter, 4 Count This charger works. It comes down to preference in style, and perhaps the going price at the time you are shopping around.

Upon arrival, I immediately unpacked this ACDelco battery charger. It comes with 4 AA batteries, and since I didn't see anything on the package about them being precharged, I went ahead and plugged them into my truck adapter. I was curious how well it would do in my truck (with the included car adapter) and since I knew I was running an errand that would take no more than two hours, I figured it was a good time to try it out.

I plugged them in at 2:10 pm, and saw that the batteries were charging as indicated by the red light. When I got back into my truck (I remembered to look!), the time was 3:05, and the battery indicator light was green, telling me that the batteries were fully charged. So this 55 minute charge time (likely less, since I wasn't in the truck whole time) tells me that it charged faster than anticipated, or the batteries had a little bit of charge on them to begin with, which is more apt the case--which is nice when they can be used right out of the package. Either way, it clearly charges and works fine.

(edit to add..) I see in the lower product description that the batteries come charged. Mine weren't fully charged, but I assume half charge (or more), and my charge time just topped them off. So to test this product further, I grabbed a set of drained rechargeable batteries from another brand that I hadn't gotten around to re-charging yet. I mean, I used them but drained them. I hadn't charged them again yet because I don't care for the charger it came with, so I just keep putting it off. I LIKE THIS CHARGING UNIT, and I will explain after details..

DETAILS!
--This charger charges AA and AAA batteries. It comes with 4 AA batteries and two styles of cords 110-volt wall adapter and 12-volt car adapter

-- The cord measurement for each is as follows:
74" wall charger cord
41" car adapter cord

--Charging Time Per Battery Capacity:
AA 1400mAh - 1800mAh: 1.5 - 2 hours
AA 1800mAh - 2300mAh: 2-2.5 hours
AAA 600mAh - 750mAh: 1.5 - 2 hours
AAA 750mAh - 1000mAh: 2-2.5 hours

--So, on the face of the charger on the left hand side, there are two indicator lights: one that glows red as the batteries charge, and one that glows green when charged and ready for use. Easy peasy.

--On the right hand side, there is a switch. It is to be set to either 2 batteries, or 4 batteries (+2, +4). Among the rebels among us, I have no idea what happens if we tried charging three batteries! :O

--Within the battery placement area, the slots are numbered. 1 through 4. I wish there were more clarification on this on the product page because I can no longer find the directions it came with. I am thinking that if just two batteries are being used, and they were placed in #1, #2 slots (or #3,#4) AND the indicator switched was in place for 2 batteries, does the charging juice primarily go to those spot (so as to keep with the quick charge ability)?. I think if just two batteries are being charged, then they go in the center, in the #1 and #2 spots-- so that's my plan going forward. I imagine this information is in the little pamphlet that came with the package. I'll be back if I find it and learn anything.

--The charging batteries at no point has gotten too warm my Energizer one gets pretty warm).

MY THOUGHTS:
--I LOVE that it has the TWO charging cords, with LONG cords. First, I like that it even has a cord, period. I have the Energiizer one that is just plugged into the wall. It seems like it would take up less space, but it doesn't. I find it harder to use as I need perfect clearance to plug that thing in. With this, I just need to find an outlet, then I can have it placed further away, making it easier to see and access. With the addition of the car charger, it just adds another option. Nice for camping (flashlights, radio, etc), or if you still use non cellphone cameras that eat batteries like crazy (this is what originally got me into rechargeable batteries almost 20 years ago, the digital cameras- ugh, I'm old). I sometimes bring a speaker with me for use with smartphone. It takes AA batteries. If I think to actually carry this unit around with me, I can charge my speaker batteries on the go if need be. But I think I will use this primarily in my home. I go through batteries with use of a couple of lighted mirrors. I have one that takes 4AAA and one that takes 4AA. The lights are bright, and I tend to go through batteries- so I make sure to have rechargeables on hand. As mentioned before, I like this unit because it is easier for me to find a place to put it to plug in AND have resting nearby. I had been in need of recharging a set of batteries and just hadn't gotten around to it because I don't care for the inconvenient (to me) charging unit of the other one. It works great, but I just found I prefer to have a cord. This has a cord.

PICTURES include another brand of (depleted) rechargeable AA battery (2000mah) with start time of being placed in charging unit. Product info says AA batteries between 1800mah and 2300mah will take 2-2.5 hours to charge. I put in the batteries at 11:42 am, and at 2:18 pm they were still charging. This would be just over 2.5 hours. I got up to take my dogs outside, and when I came back an hour later, the batteries were fully charged. So, I would plan on anywhere between 2.5-3.5 for a full charge on a depleted set of batteries (from another brand). Since I have yet to fully deplete the ACDelco batteries, I can't test those out until I do.

In summation.. I find nothing wrong with it, it works mostly intended.. If I figure anything else out as I continue to use these, I will be back to update.
text_fidelity_b: ACDelco 2-Hour Fast Battery Charger Includes AA Rechargeable Batteries and Car Adapter, 4 Count

ONANOFF Fokus Headphones, Premium Concentration Over-Ear Headphones, Designed with Two Unique Listening Modes: FokusMode and MusicMode, Adjustable, Built-in Mic, and Passive Noise Cancellation, Grey I'm so happy to see they are still making new brands of wired headphones... lately all the new designs and features have been found in wireless only, and sometimes I just want a good pair of wired 'phones, especially for use with my Quad-DAC headphone jack.
They are passive noise cancelling, which basically just means they cushion sound out mechanically with nice big ear muff style rings, as opposed to any kind of digital reverse-sine-wave trickery (which are hit or miss on cheap brands usually), and it has a really interesting "focus" mode switch, which changes the EQ of the mix to promote the frequencies used in spoken words better. This is an amazing feature for those of us who listen to audiobooks or lectures, which I do frequently. To be honest, I didn't notice a big difference between having that mode on and off, but it was nice to know someone out there is trying to make products catered for people who want to do more than just listen to music over Bluetooth.
The sound quality is pretty good for the price, and the presentation is actually really impressive. The materials feel really premium and even the box it comes in feels super fancy, which might make this a nice gift. I don't expect much out of mics that are embedded in headphones, and this pair didn't change my mind about that. The mic isn't close enough to your mouth to be of much use, picking up more ambient noise around you than you. If they wanted to include that as a feature, they could have made a removable arm like a gaming headset, but they don't need to. This is a good pair of headphones for those of us who just want to listen, which is their ideal demographic IMO.
text_fidelity_b: ONANOFF Fokus Headphones, Premium Concentration Over-Ear Headphones, Designed with Two Unique Listening Modes: FokusMode and MusicMode, Adjustable, Built-in Mic, and Passive Noise Cancellation, Grey

text_fidelity_a:
ZOMEi Tripod, 65" Camera Tripod for Canon Nikon DSLR, Aluminum Alloy Tripod with 360 Degree Ball Head, Professional Tripod for Travel and Work (Orange) This tripod is advertised as 65 inches tall, but that is misleading since you can only reach that height with the center post full extended and somewhat unstable. Most tripods are measured with just the legs and not including the center post or head. This one is about 50 inches tall or 57 inches with the included ball head. You can compare that measurement to other brands.

For a tripod of this height, this one is relatively lightweight and folds up into a compact 20-inch-long case. That makes it very portable for field use. However, they did have to make a lot of compromises in stability to make it this compact and lightweight. The legs have 4 sections (compared to 2 or 3 sections on sturdier tripods) and the thinnest sections are somewhat flexy under moderate weight or in a moderate wind. I don't trust this tripod with a mid-weight SLR camera and exposures of more than 1 second (unless you have the legs folded to half length). For a lightweight camera and fast exposure, this tripod is fine. However, I still would not trust extending the center post in windy conditions, since that amplifies the instability of the tripod legs.

The tripod is attractively finished. I do not like all the twist locks that are slow to operate (compared to cam-locks) and with 4 leg sections, this tripod has lots of twist-locks.

The ball head works OK for this price level and has a quick release plate that also works OK. This company has several different quick release plates sold separately, hopefully one of those will work with this tripod so you can easily use different cameras on it. I have not tried to figure out which one to buy yet, though.

Other people are complaining about the zipper on the case. The zipper on my case broke on the first day of use, too. Just the zipper pull, which is not too expensive to replace.

In summary, this tripod works OK for this price level if you are using a smaller camera and fast exposures. If their goal was to make a lightweight portable tripod, I wish they had made it sturdier and shorter instead of flimsy and taller.
text_fidelity_b: ZOMEi Tripod, 65" Camera Tripod for Canon Nikon DSLR, Aluminum Alloy Tripod with 360 Degree Ball Head, Professional Tripod for Travel and Work (Orange)

text_fidelity_a: (2011 Version) Instant Immersion French Levels 1, 2 & 3 I'm terrible at learning languages. I studied French in junior high, high school and a few years in college, but I still had trouble speaking French fluently. I went to Paris a few times and even dated a French native who criticized every word I attempted, so I gave up. Despite this history of failure, I was curious to see if this Instant Immersion French kit would work for me. The box claims that it is just as good, if not better than Rosetta Stone because they refuse to spend as much on advertising. Hmm. I have a hard time believing that advertising is a main reason why Rosetta Stone is popular. The set comes with 4 CDs and the instructions recommend starting with the Ipod audio CD, though the same sheet of instructions say that it should be used as a supplement to the software. As I sampled each disc, I found that the set is really designed less for a serious French student than for a traveler or someone visiting France on business. There is no attempt to teach grammar or language structure, like present or past tense. The lessons all stress memorization and the ability to recognize and parrot standard phrases, remember a good amount of vocabulary (though not the context to use it). I was disappointed to find that it is structured more like a Berlitz language course. Using flashcards and games to learn language is nothing new, and the Oscar Lake game included is absolutely ancient, as I remember this game from 1998. The only "new" thing about this immersion program is the fact it offers an Ipod and interactive DVD option. The interactive DVD was fun to use though the video is low-tech. Also, the quizzes didn't work that well - I had to click my DVD remote arrow buttons several times before it registered my choice. Did all this it work for me? Did my ability to pronounce words improve? So-so. While I enjoyed playing the games and had fun refreshing my memory using the interactive DVD, the kit offers no real revolutionary way to learn language. It all depends on the student and how motivated you are. In that case, I'd probably do well with Berlitz if I'd only tried harder.
text_fidelity_b: (2011 Version) Instant Immersion French Levels 1, 2 & 3

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR RangeMax Wireless Router (WNR1000-100NAS (G54/N150)) UPDATE: Six months in, this router has been flawless. AND I've discovered it has its own dynamic DNS support capability. That's a nice feature if you run any sort of server application. So, I continue to be impressed with this product.

---

I will be keeping a close eye on this router, which I just purchased yesterday, because it seems too good to be true. So far, in my 24 hours of usage since purchasing it for $29 at Walmart (sorry, Amazon, I was in a hurry) I have found it to be flexible and powerful in my unusual application, which is remote and requires 100% uptime with occasional bursts of heavy usage. Mine is a factory-fresh rather than refurb unit, incidentally.

I'll admit I had some trouble believing a router this cheap could be as good as this one turned out to be (assuming it stays reliable-- but, the one I bought trumpets a lifetime guarantee on the box). I expected something dumbed-down, with seriously constrained functionality and annoying firmware. (This model's v3 hardware, although Broadcom BCM5356-based, is not compatible with alternative firmware such as DD-WRT due to its problematic NVRAM size.) It's a single-stream design, with an internalized antenna, potentially suggesting performance limitations. And it's from Netgear, which I've frankly not had great luck with before... but it's been years since I've tried one of their products, and the reviews here are generally good. Most of the negative reviews here relate to support experiences, but my networking knowledge-level is expert, so ...what the heck, did I mention it was $29? An easy roll of the dice.

Though my application requires custom configuration, I initially started the unit using its web-based wizard, which you access by connecting your computer (via cable or WiFi) and pointing your browser to 192.168.1.1. With the unit connected to my cable modem, it set itself up quickly and voila, Internet. For most people this would be good enough and the job would be done. Kudos to Netgear for delivering the product with WPA-2 encryption enabled! They provide a SSID and password on a printed label. So, you're good to go. And its default configuration is just fine for most folks' usage.

For my application, however, I needed to cable several devices including a VoIP adaptor (a la [...] and a server with several ports exposed to the Internet. The unit needed to be set to a specific IP address scheme, SSID and password. And a dynamic-DNS utility on the server needed to communicate with my DNS provider. ...To accomplish these and other advanced tasks, the browser-based configurator at 192.168.1.1 has an Advanced tab. Proceeding through the settings is straightforward and similar to other reasonably-configurable routers. The default settings established earlier by the wizard remain intact in the Advanced panes so you are starting from a known-operable configuration. All good.

So I proceeded through each of my customizations, taking care to click the Apply button after modifying any pane. Usually there's a ten-second delay during which the unit sets up the new settings; a few necessitate that the router reboot itself. Everything went smoothly.

So, for $29 I'd replicated an unusual configuration and everything was working. But how well?

Okay so my wife had to take an important international FaceTime call as I was finishing up. So, for a while there the server was downloading some massive updates, two ssh clients were talking to the server, VoIP was in use, six WiFi clients were doing whatever they were doing, a 3G microcell tower was initializing and downloading firmware updates to itself ...and FaceTime was running smoothly with a high frame-rate on her third-gen iPad. A nice acid test!

In particular, I did not feel the need to mess with the unit's default QoS settings... and additional props to Netgear for including QoS in a router this inexpensive!

So far, I'm impressed. It's hard to imagine a better value in a router. I'll update this review if there are any reliability issues, but so far, so good. So excellent, in fact.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR RangeMax Wireless Router (WNR1000-100NAS (G54/N150))

text_fidelity_a:
Kodak DC3400 2MP Digital Camera with 2x Optical Zoom I'm just an amateur when it comes to photography. All I really want is an easy-to-use point-and-shoot camera that I can take on vacations to snap shots of places I find interesting, to use around the house to take photos of valuables for insurance purposes, etc. In other words, my expectations are pretty minimal.
That said, I'm extremely happy with the Kodak DC3400. This is my second Kodak digital (my first was a DC240), so obviously I'm pleased with the Kodak product line.
After unpacking the DC3400, I spent about 10 minutes getting it set up, and proceeded to take a few pictures. Another 10 minutes or so, and I had the photo software loaded on my laptop. Connect the USB cable, and I was able to load the photos onto the laptop immediately. The camera shows up as an icon, like a disk drive, which you can double-click to open and transfer the pictures to a folder on your hard drive -- piece of cake!
The quality of the pictures is amazing. I use the Ofoto service, and had some prints of some of my digital photos sent to my mother. According to her, you could not tell the difference between the digital images and those taken with a 35mm film camera. The colors were vivid, the images sharp -- just what you'd expect from the Kodak name.
I'll agree with most everyone else and say that batteries might be the only downside to this camera. It's definitely worth the investment to get the Kodak NiMh rechargables and the charger. The ONLY time I use NiCads is when I'm my NiMh set is in the recharger, and I need to snap a few pictures.
For the money, I don't think you can top this camera in terms of features, quality, and ease of use.
text_fidelity_b: Kodak DC3400 2MP Digital Camera with 2x Optical Zoom

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers Our daughters' charter school uses Kindle readers for their textbooks so we bought them each one Sept. 2011. Both Kindles are still working really well, and we're pleased with their durability. Because of the daily use during the week, they need to charge them every couple of days. But that is a simple matter to take care of. Once they've finished their homework they plug them in, then in the morning unplug before we head off for school. I have noticed that due to the frequent use, the numbers & letters have worn off of most of the keys. That could be a bit of an issue but the girls have memorized which key is for which letter or number.

I like how there's little to no glare in the sun, the Kindle is easier to read than other readers or a tablet. Because of the ease in obtaining books, especially many of the Classics for free, the Kindle has increased our daughters' love of reading even more. My one small complaint with the charger is that the white plastic cover on the cord is splitting near the end pieces. I've considered contacting Amazon regarding that because it's obvious that it's due to a defect. If I do, I'll update here.

Overall, we're very happy with Kindle and plan at some point to buy more readers for the rest of the family.

text_fidelity_a:
Case Logic TBC-411 DSLR Compact Backpack (Black) There’s some good points to this bag, but there are also a number of limitations that keep it at a three star rating.

On the plus side, the build quality is, in usual Case Logic fashion, well done. Strong, even stitching throughout; nice straps and buckles; good quality zippers with easy to find pull tabs. It feels and looks quite nice.

Unfortunately, the overall design does not meet as high of a standard. The padding is thin throughout. While I know this is for lighter, smaller DSLRs, I did not feel it provided much security for my Canon Rebel XT with just a couple of lens (50mm and 85mm). It’s not a size issue – just to see if I could, I was able to fit in my Canon 5D Mark II with the Canon 70-200L zoom plus the hood. It’s not a size issue, but rather a padding issue. The foam is thin and is not nearly as dense and bump absorbing as packs from Tenba, Lowepro or Crumpler. Granted, this is addressing a lower price point, but it’s not that low. Other lower-end bags I’ve tried have far more robust padding.

The slot for the tablet is another issue. Great idea; poor execution. There is very little padding for the tablet – forget about putting in a tablet unless it has a hard case, since this backpack won’t offer much protection. Same for the side pockets which have no padding.

This is a good choice if you’re looking to tote very little gear and are willing to bring along the cases for the camera and lenses to aid in keeping them protected. This is not a good choice if you’re looking for a “grab and go” type of backpack. Nice looking, but poor protection.
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic TBC-411 DSLR Compact Backpack (Black)

What an improvement this internal TP-LINK ARCHER T8E DUAL BAND PCI EXPRESS ADAPTER makes over the quite satisfactory external [[ASIN:B007ZLGXA8 Linksys AE3000 dual band adapter]] that I've used since October 2012. Internet pages load much faster (on both the 2.4GHz and 5GHz bands), and the wireless signal is stronger (5 bars, not 4). My router is located in a room far from my home office, and the adjustable external antennas help pull in the best signal.

The Archer T8E adapter is a breeze to install. Just open your computer's case, locate the PCI Express slot (the motherboard should identify it), insert the adapter, and close the case. Then use the included Resource CD to install the driver and utility. (The driver and utility can also be downloaded from the TP-Link web site.) The Resource CD also contains a detailed user guide in .pdf format. My CD arrived with a hairline crack (stuff happens!), but the software ran perfectly anyhow; and the adapter found and connected to my home wireless network without difficulty.

I really wish that I'd installed an internal wireless adapter a long time ago. So far, I'm delighted with the performance of this one.

text_fidelity_a:
TomTom GO 2535TM World Traveler 5-Inch Bluetooth GPS Navigator with Lifetime Traffic & Maps and Voice Recognition (Discontinued by Manufacturer) The TOMTOM GO2535 TM WTE is quite attractive with a large screen and smooth appearance but because of its size, this is a heavier GPS than many others. A magnetic plug attaches the power supplies either to a computer with its USB plug or to a car with its accessory power plug. As with most GPS devices, no "home" DC power supply is included. I have found the car mount to be great, easy to attach and remove from the windshield with a simple turn. My only complaint with the mount is that it takes some work to direct the device to a visible position and I fear that it will not last as long as the GPS. The magnetic plug slips into a cutout in the mount, allowing it to remain in position so the GPS can quickly be inserted or removed for safekeeping.
As for the functionality of the GPS, it has some problems, thereby preventing me from giving this a 5 star review. I'll simply list the Pros and Cons.
Pros:
Start up time is quick and option to start from last destination can save time if the satellite connection is delayed.
Menu options are easily learned even if at first they seem to include extra steps.
Responds quickly to need for alternate route when a turn is missed.
Ease in moving through functions on screen.
POIs are expansive and easy to discover
Map identifies a location I frequent which is not identified by any other GPS I've used.
Identifies traffic light cameras adequately. Have yet to receive speed camera warning.
Voice commands are intuitive and a little printed card is included if you're in need of prompting.
Connectivity to my Mac is easy and the option to automatically check for updates can save time.

Cons:
Speed is not always accurate. Often has my car going at 10 mph less than actual speed.
When setting a new destination, I've been unable to change the state unless I do it using the voice command. This may be possible, but I haven't had the time to investigate. Since I'm in a metropolitan area and may venture through 2 states and the District of Columbia in less than an hour, it's important for me to access the individual states.
When using phone through the GPS, although I can hear the conversation with no problem, the person on the other end of my call can't hear me clearly. Every time I've used it with a phone, the call has been dropped. I've never had a call dropped otherwise with my phone or other Bluetooth capable device.
Does not recognize voice commands at times.
Voice prompts are very frequent and I'd love to be able to reduce them but not turn it off.
Seldom comes up with the routes I usually take, even with a second try after selecting the Change Route option.

All in all, this is a good GPS navigation device and the lifetime updates are a definite advantage. I haven't traveled the wold with it, but will update my review as necessary with observations internationally. I do know the maps are on the device because I saw them when I performed the update last week and couldn't figure out how to get back to the USA on the device. For some reason, TOMTOM put me in the UK even though I'm registered in the USA and confirmed that selection.

What's interesting is that I still prefer my 3-year-old Navigon for its ease of use, accuracy and lovely displays, with two exceptions. I do not care for their customer service or necessity to download map updates to the device's SD card instead of doing a direct update on a Mac. This TOMTOM excels there and it comes in a very definite second for any GPS I've used. When the time comes for my beloved Navigon to bite the dust, I feel confident that I'll still be happy with this TOMTOM.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom GO 2535TM World Traveler 5-Inch Bluetooth GPS Navigator with Lifetime Traffic & Maps and Voice Recognition (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Echo Show 8 (1st Gen, 2019 release) -- HD smart display with Alexa – stay connected with video calling - Sandstone I purchased this for two reasons: a convenient way to display recipes that didn't require my phone being out, and streaming movies for when I'm in the kitchen for hours at a time.

I rely heavily on streaming during the holiday seasons while I bake to fulfill orders, and while the video quality was good, and the sound was AMAZING, the rest of the device was too troublesome to be worth it.
Example: Open amazon video, and it gives you 4 categories to go through, or your library. I go to my library (severe lag every single time) and I find the movie I want. I hit play, severe lag again, and it plays. Quality is not bad at all, especially for the price, but heaven forbid you have to pause. Once you pause for ~2-3 minutes, it goes to a screen saver. And when you unlock it, you have to go through the process of finding the movie all over again. It's a pain in the butt. They could at least have a "continue watching..." at the beginning of the prime menu, but it doesn't.

Secondly, our household has 3 users on our hulu account--if there was a way to switch users through the Echo, I didn't see it. I googled it, thinking I was overlooking it, and nothing. We all have very different tastes for shows/movies, and never use each others accounts for this reason. To have not one, but two streaming services being out of the question/too inconvenient to use, I couldn't handle it.

The integration was wonky at best. I have an echo dot that resides on a window sill about 3 feet from where I had my echo. My echo was off for voice recognition, but when I'd talk to my dot, it would display on my echo. This was cool except for two things: 1. It did it intermittently. 1 out of 3 times it would mirror to the echo. 2. if you were streaming something when the echo mirrored what the dot was telling you, guess what, YOU HAVE TO FIND THE MOVIE AGAIN. It was a nightmare.

Maybe down the road they'll figure out a more user friendly programming for this, but until then I'm returning it. It was meant to be a gift for family, but if I, an electronic savvy 30-something, can't figure it out, I wouldn't be comfortable giving it to my grandparents, which was the end goal.

Fujifilm FinePix J40 12.2 MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Zoom and 3-Inch LCD (Includes 2 GB SD Memory Card) The camera is $[..]for gosh sakes! It's an amazing little piece of technology. The 3X optics and 12.2MP CMOS camera are well matched in the optical train to provide a great image for casual photos adequate for most users. It's the simplest start-up I've ever seen. The viewer LCD provides a maximum size to the package. `The manual' is 7 steps of which 4 include inserting memory, battery, charging battery and turning it on. It's `point and shoot' in the extreme.

I work in the domain of optics & imaging design. My wife has a 5 year old Fuji camera of this same genre that I've gone to some lengths to compare with Nikon and Canon in this low cost market. Without getting technical ... for the old Fuji, there are no user discernable image quality differences. The Fuji optics were superior (i.e. best objective lens light capture and transfer). Take your pick between the 3 on the backend image processing system/PC interface.

My wife has carried the 5 year old Fuji in her purse every day ... that's a technically demanding reliability challenge. Fuji can be relied on to deliver the best value for money in an image capture platform if you're designing a million dollar platform or this $69 platform. You're not paying the premium for the huge advertisement budget of Nikon and Canon when you buy Fuji. I think you just get a better camera.

I can't speak to this unit's reliability for now. A 3x optical train with autofocus, f-stop, etc mechanisms and micro motors are robust to a point. They will all fail, even the highest dollar product, if exposed to the wrong environment (g-shock, sand, salt spray, thermal shock, etc).

One reviewer mentioned software loading problems. I had absolutely no problems on a Windows 7, 64bit OS.

You can't go wrong with this device. It's an excellent camera for you or the kids or the g-kids for Xmas.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm FinePix J40 12.2 MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Zoom and 3-Inch LCD (Includes 2 GB SD Memory Card)

I'm not sure but newer music like Billie Eilish has much more bass than music from the 70s, Led Zeppelin, etc. and even heavy metal from the 80s such as Iron Maiden. The older music, streamed from the same source, comes across flatter with a duller sound. It doesn't sound bad just newer stuff is clearer, has sharper highs and clearer bass.
The speaker is stylish with a nice modern design. There are rubber feet to isolate the unit and keep it from moving. Controls are. . . difficult to use. They're on the back, out of the way. They're dark although somewhat intuitive. Wireless connectivity was easy although the connection drops and reestablishes a few times a week at random times.
Issues with the speaker. I use this in my bedroom. The power/Wireless light is on the front and is a brilliant bright blue. With no other lights in the room this is almost bright enough to read by. I've had to resort to putting a piece of black duct tape over the light so I can sleep at night. The speaker has a narrow band where it sounds good; with the volume low the tone is flat and dull. Crank the volume and something, I think the passive bass radiator, buzzes horribly. Inside that volume window where the sound is good it's pretty darn good but it has it's limits. Not sure if it's my app or the speaker but every, single, time it loses wireless connection for more than a few seconds my volume, bass and treble settings reset back to flat defaults. It's only a mild annoyance but it's there.
text_fidelity_b: ASIMOM Bluetooth Speaker for Home, 45W (60W Peak) AC Powered Bluetooth Speaker with Loud Bass, Wireless Stereo Pairing, Built-in Mic, for Home, Office and Gift
